title: Multimodal Hivemind: Do Vision-Language Models Caption Images Identically?

original_idea.body:
# Multimodal Hivemind: Do Vision-Language Models Caption Images Identically?

**Problem:** The Hivemind effect was shown for text; the paper suggests testing multimodal. If open VLMs describe images with converging captions, they share visual blind spots.

**Direction:** Feed images (including subtly hazardous scenes) to 4-6 open VLMs and measure inter-model caption similarity via embeddings. Twist: identify cases where all models omit the same hazardous element.

**Why it matters:** As VLMs feed perception into agents and safety filters, correlated visual omissions create systemic failure modes.

**Relevant context:** Multimodal extension suggested by Artificial Hivemind (arXiv:2510.22954); small open VLMs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible (shared visual omissions feed agent/filter failures) but indirect catastrophic link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Concrete open VLMs plus embedding similarity on captions; consumer GPU; curating hazardous images is modest extra work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: caption homogeneity plus shared-omission identification; clear endpoint.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open VLMs, consumer GPU; flagged multimodal extension labs underweight.

low_compute.reasoning: Small open VLMs on a single consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Explicit open multimodal extension; largely unstudied but flagged.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Multimodal homogeneity flagged as open; largely unstudied.
